strikes.title: FBI Says North Korean Hackers Stole Over $400 Million in Crypto Using Deepfake Video Calls
strikes.location: United States (victims worldwide)
strikes.data_affected: Cryptocurrency funds and executive identity (voice/face)
strikes.impact: Over $400 million in crypto stolen from exchanges and funds via social engineering.
strikes.prevention: Verify high-value transfer requests out-of-band, require dual authorization, and train staff to treat unexpected video calls as untrusted.
strikes.summary: State-backed operators impersonated executives on deepfake video calls to trick employees into approving fraudulent cryptocurrency transfers worth hundreds of millions of dollars.

strikes.title: SilentAir Hijacks Asian Telecom Networks to Intercept SMS 2FA Codes and Spy on Taiwanese Users
strikes.location: Taiwan
strikes.data_affected: SMS one-time codes, 2FA tokens and private communications
strikes.impact: Telecom networks hijacked to intercept 2FA codes and spy on targeted Taiwanese users.
strikes.prevention: Replace SMS 2FA with phishing-resistant (FIDO2) MFA, and harden and monitor signalling (SS7/Diameter) interconnects.
strikes.summary: A stealthy group compromised telecom infrastructure to intercept SMS one-time codes, defeating 2FA and enabling surveillance of targeted users.

strikes.title: Operation Endgame Takes Down Gootloader, CastleRAT and StealC Servers, Seizes 6.4M Stolen Logins
strikes.location: Europe (coordinated takedown)
strikes.data_affected: 6.4 million stolen logins and session tokens
strikes.impact: Info-stealer botnets (Gootloader, CastleRAT, StealC) seized; 6.4M credentials recovered.
strikes.prevention: Rotate credentials exposed to info-stealers, enforce MFA everywhere, and block execution of unsigned loaders on endpoints.
strikes.summary: An international law-enforcement operation dismantled malware infrastructure and recovered millions of stolen credentials harvested by info-stealers.

strikes.title: Trezor Confirms Hidden Implants in CryptoBilis-Sold Wallets That Can Steal Recovery Phrases
strikes.location: Czechia (global customers)
strikes.data_affected: Cryptocurrency wallet recovery phrases / private keys
strikes.impact: Resold hardware wallets carried implants able to steal recovery phrases and drain funds.
strikes.prevention: Buy hardware wallets only from the vendor or authorised sellers, and verify tamper-evidence and firmware signatures before first use.
strikes.summary: Tampered hardware wallets sold through a third-party reseller contained hidden implants capable of exfiltrating users' recovery phrases.

strikes.title: How Fake Job Interviews Helped Hackers Pull Off a $6.3 Billion Crypto Heist
strikes.location: United Arab Emirates (global crypto firms)
strikes.data_affected: Developer workstations, signing keys and cryptocurrency funds
strikes.impact: Fake-recruiter malware led to a multi-billion-dollar cryptocurrency heist.
strikes.prevention: Verify recruiters and candidates out-of-band, run coding tasks only in isolated throwaway VMs, and protect signing keys with hardware and multi-signature.
strikes.summary: Operatives used fake job interviews and malicious coding tasks to plant malware on developers at crypto firms, enabling one of the largest cryptocurrency thefts on record.

strikes.title: GTA 6 hacker pleads guilty after release from secure hospital
strikes.location: Rockstar Games, headquartered in New York, USA (victim organization); attacker was UK-based.
strikes.data_affected: Confidential GTA 6 game footage and source code, along with data from other targeted organizations (not fully disclosed in this report).
strikes.impact: Rockstar Games suffered a significant, high-profile leak of unreleased intellectual property for its flagship title GTA 6. The scale of reputational and commercial damage to Rockstar/Take-Two Interactive was substantial; full financial impact not disclosed.
strikes.prevention: Enforce strict access controls and zero-trust network segmentation to prevent unauthorized users from reaching sensitive development repositories and internal Slack/Confluence environments used to stage the breach.
strikes.summary: Arion Kurtaj, a then-teenager and member of the Lapsus$ group, hacked Rockstar Games and leaked confidential GTA 6 footage and source code, along with carrying out additional breaches. He has now pleaded guilty to the Rockstar Games hack and related offences following his release from a secure hospital.

strikes.title: SANSAR Linux Cryptomining Malware Uses Modified NVIDIA Library to Hide GPU Activity
strikes.location: Linux-based systems targeted globally; specific victim country not disclosed in the report.
strikes.data_affected: Linux system resources (CPU and GPU compute capacity); NVIDIA GPU telemetry/library readings manipulated to mask mining activity.
strikes.impact: Victim organizations running Linux systems with NVIDIA GPUs had their computing resources hijacked for cryptocurrency mining; the precise number of affected organizations or financial scale is not disclosed in the report.
strikes.prevention: Deploy integrity monitoring and application allowlisting on Linux hosts to detect unauthorized modification of system libraries (such as the NVIDIA GPU library), which would flag the tampered binaries used to conceal mining workloads.
strikes.summary: A financially motivated threat cluster (REF3364) deployed SANSAR, a Rust-based Linux malware toolkit, to run covert cryptocurrency mining operations on compromised hosts. SANSAR tampers with NVIDIA GPU library readings to conceal high GPU workloads and communicates with operators over the TOR network to manage both CPU and GPU miners.

strikes.title: Amazon Uncovers AI Agent Campaign Targeting LiteLLM, Dify, and Other Apps for API Keys
strikes.location: Internet-exposed AI applications globally; campaign activity captured via Amazon decoy (honeypot) servers.
strikes.data_affected: AI provider API keys stored within internet-exposed AI applications (LiteLLM, One API, Dify, and others).
strikes.impact: Multiple internet-exposed AI platforms targeted globally; stolen API keys were actively weaponized to fund and expand the campaign, enabling unauthorized use of AI model services. Full scale of victim organizations not disclosed.
strikes.prevention: Restrict AI application admin interfaces and API key stores from public internet exposure; enforce network-level access controls (e.g., firewall rules, VPN-only access) so that API key management endpoints are never reachable by unauthenticated external actors.
strikes.summary: Attackers deployed AI agents to scan internet-exposed AI applications — including LiteLLM, One API, and Dify — for vulnerabilities in order to steal stored AI provider API keys. Amazon's threat intelligence team captured the attackers' own agent logs via decoy servers, revealing that stolen keys were then recycled to power further reconnaissance and key-harvesting operations.

strikes.title: BO Team Exploits Log4Shell in VMware vCenter, Compromises Russian Firm's Code-Signing Server
strikes.location: Russian software development firm's internal network and development infrastructure, Russia.
strikes.data_affected: Software development infrastructure and a code-signing server, including signed software artifacts potentially usable for downstream supply-chain attacks.
strikes.impact: A named Russian software development firm suffered a prolonged, months-long compromise of its core development environment and code-signing capabilities; the full downstream impact on software distributed by the developer was not disclosed in the report.
strikes.prevention: Apply the Log4Shell patch (Log4j 2.17.1+) immediately and enforce network segmentation to isolate critical build and code-signing infrastructure from internet-facing or externally accessible services such as VMware vCenter.
strikes.summary: Threat actor BO Team (aka Black Owl, Hoody Hyena) exploited the Log4Shell vulnerability (CVE-2021-44228) in VMware vCenter to compromise the development infrastructure and code-signing server of a Russian software developer over a period of several months. The intrusion was discovered during an investigation by Kaspersky's ICS CERT team after the affected developer sought assistance in June 2025.

strikes.title: Cursor Says Stolen Fireworks AI Key Led to Trojanized Claude Code Extension Incident
strikes.location: Cursor's extension marketplace (US-based AI code editor platform), with the initial key exposure originating at Fireworks AI (also US-based)
strikes.data_affected: Cursor-issued access key stored at Fireworks AI; read-only data accessed via that key; integrity of the Claude Code extension package on Cursor's marketplace
strikes.impact: Cursor users who installed or updated the Claude Code extension were exposed to a trojanized version; full scale of downstream user impact not disclosed in the report.
strikes.prevention: Implement short-lived, scoped API keys with automatic rotation and immediate revocation workflows so that a key exposed at a third-party vendor cannot be leveraged to modify or replace published extension artifacts.
strikes.summary: An attacker stole an access key that Cursor had issued to Fireworks AI following a breach at Fireworks AI, then used it to copy data and trojanize Anthropic's official Claude Code extension on Cursor's extension marketplace. The compromise resulted in a malicious version of the extension being distributed to Cursor users.

strikes.title: Attackers Exploit UnrealIRCd Flaw That Enables Server-Level Command Injection
strikes.location: Internet-facing UnrealIRCd IRC server deployments globally; CISA KEV advisory scoped primarily to US federal and critical infrastructure environments.
strikes.data_affected: UnrealIRCd open-source IRC server instances; server-level command execution capability exposed, potentially compromising the host operating environment and all data accessible to the IRC server process.
strikes.impact: Any organization or individual running a vulnerable UnrealIRCd deployment is at risk of full server-level compromise. Scale of active exploitation is not disclosed in the report, but CISA's KEV listing signals confirmed, widespread-enough exploitation to warrant urgent remediation across the US federal and broader IT community.
strikes.prevention: Apply the vendor-issued patch or upgrade UnrealIRCd to the fixed version immediately; if patching is not immediately possible, restrict IRC server exposure by enforcing strict network-level access controls (firewall rules) to limit who can send delimiter-bearing input to the service.
strikes.summary: CISA added a high-severity command-injection flaw in UnrealIRCd (tracked as CVE-2026-114713, CVSS 8.6) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after reports of active in-the-wild exploitation. The vulnerability stems from improper neutralization of delimiters, enabling server-level command injection against IRC server instances.

strikes.title: Hackers Exploit PHP2Shell Flaws in Check Point Gateways to Deploy TSGA Backdoor and Wipe ESXi Files
strikes.location: Israeli organizations running Check Point Security Gateways with Gaia OS
strikes.data_affected: Check Point Security Gateway systems running Gaia OS; ESXi virtual machine files wiped; backdoor (TSGA) deployed for persistent access.
strikes.impact: Israeli organizations were targeted; attackers achieved initial access, privilege escalation, persistent backdoor installation, and destructive wiping of ESXi files. Full scale of affected organizations not disclosed.
strikes.prevention: Apply all available patches and hotfixes for Check Point Security Gateways immediately, specifically those addressing the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities, to eliminate the initial access vector exploited in this campaign.
strikes.summary: An unknown threat actor exploited PHP2Shell vulnerabilities in unpatched Check Point Security Gateways, combined with a previously unreported local privilege escalation flaw in Gaia OS, to deploy a backdoor named TSGA and wipe ESXi files. The campaign began on October 30, 2026, and was observed targeting Israeli organizations, with a broader follow-up phase reported by Check Point.

strikes.title: Hackers Exploit N-central Flaws to Infect 21 Servers, Including 19 Running Hotfix 2
strikes.location: N-able N-central managed servers at affected customer sites (ground zero not geographically specified; vendor headquartered in Canada).
strikes.data_affected: N-central managed servers; systems running N-central software including those patched with Hotfix 2 were compromised.
strikes.impact: 21 servers infected across N-central customer environments, including 19 that had already applied Hotfix 2, indicating the patch was insufficient; N-able restricted platform functionality as a precautionary measure, potentially disrupting managed service provider (MSP) operations.
strikes.prevention: Apply vendor-issued patches and security advisories immediately upon release, and implement network-level controls (e.g., firewall rules restricting access to N-central management interfaces) to limit exposure of management platforms to only trusted IP ranges.
strikes.summary: Hackers exploited newly disclosed vulnerabilities in N-able's N-central product, tracked as 4EverAble2Shell and Agent2Shell, compromising 21 servers — 19 of which were running the latest Hotfix 2. N-able responded by restricting certain N-central features and integrations while remediation is completed.

strikes.title: 186 Fake AI Domains Redirect Users to ClickFix Lures, Browser Malware, and Search Hijackers
strikes.location: End users globally redirected via 186 fake AI-tool lookalike domains; ground zero is not tied to a single country — attacker infrastructure origin not disclosed.
strikes.data_affected: Browser settings, search engine configurations, and potentially broader system access via browser-hijacking malware and malicious extensions installed on victims' devices.
strikes.impact: End users seeking legitimate AI tools were redirected to malicious lookalike domains; affected individuals risk browser hijacking, search engine manipulation, and malware infection. Scale of confirmed victim count is not disclosed.
strikes.prevention: Enable and enforce DNS filtering or a secure web gateway to block newly registered lookalike domains, preventing users from reaching typosquatted AI-tool URLs before malicious content is served.
strikes.summary: Cybersecurity researchers at Island identified a campaign dubbed "TypoPrompting" in which 186 lookalike domains impersonating popular AI tools serve ClickFix-style verification lures, browser-hijacking malware, and search-hijacking extensions to users who mistype AI tool URLs. The delivery pattern redirects victims into malicious prompts designed to trigger malware installation or browser compromise.

strikes.title: SCKit Malware Turns ScreenConnect Support Sessions Into Potential MSP Attack Paths
strikes.location: ConnectWise ScreenConnect deployments, primarily targeting managed service providers (MSPs); ConnectWise is headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, USA.
strikes.data_affected: ConnectWise ScreenConnect remote access sessions; MSP environments and their downstream managed endpoints accessible via hijacked support sessions.
strikes.impact: MSPs and their downstream clients are at risk of full compromise through hijacked ScreenConnect support sessions; exact number of affected organizations not disclosed.
strikes.prevention: Immediately apply the available patch for CVE-2026-84869 on all ConnectWise ScreenConnect deployments and audit active support sessions for unauthorized access or anomalous lateral movement.
strikes.summary: An ongoing campaign exploits CVE-2026-84869 (CVSS 9.9), a now-patched critical flaw in ConnectWise ScreenConnect, deploying the SCKit malware toolkit to hijack remote support sessions and create attack paths into managed service providers (MSPs). Blackpoint Cyber's Adversary Pursuit Group recovered the attacker toolkit and shared details with The Hacker News.

strikes.title: Calendar Invites and Live Proxies: Inside a Google Session Hijacking Campaign
strikes.location: Corporate users globally; specific ground-zero country not disclosed — Google LLC headquartered in the United States.
strikes.data_affected: Live Google session tokens (authenticated user sessions) of corporate users.
strikes.impact: Multiple corporate users had their active Google sessions hijacked, potentially granting attackers persistent, authenticated access to their Google accounts and associated services. Hundreds of attacker domains were involved, indicating a broad-scale campaign; exact number of victims not disclosed.
strikes.prevention: Enforce hardware-bound session credentials or FIDO2/passkey-based authentication so that stolen session tokens cannot be replayed by an attacker from a different device or origin.
strikes.summary: Since mid-August 2026, a phishing campaign dubbed Operation CloudFire has been targeting corporate users to steal live Google session tokens, using calendar invites and live proxies to bypass standard link-inspection defenses. Material Security's Threat Research team identified the operation and took down hundreds of attacker domains in response.

strikes.title: Attacker Used 4,837 Hijacked GitHub Accounts to Run a CI Secret Stealer in 1,806+ Repositories
strikes.location: GitHub platform (repositories globally); attacker entry point via GitHub's hosted infrastructure.
strikes.data_affected: CI/CD pipeline secrets, cloud credentials, and repository environment variables across 1,806+ GitHub repositories.
strikes.impact: At least 1,806 GitHub repositories were actively compromised; secrets and cloud credentials accessible to their CI workflows were likely exfiltrated. The full scope of downstream damage to organizations owning those repositories was not disclosed at time of reporting.
strikes.prevention: Enforce short-lived, scoped CI secrets using OIDC-based cloud authentication (e.g., GitHub Actions OIDC tokens) instead of long-lived static credentials stored as repository secrets, so that even if a workflow is hijacked the stolen tokens expire rapidly and have minimal blast radius.
strikes.summary: An attacker leveraged stolen credentials for 4,837 GitHub accounts to inject a secret-stealing payload into repositories those accounts had write access to. The malicious code ran inside CI/CD workflows across at least 1,806 repositories, harvesting secrets and cloud credentials reachable by those pipelines.

strikes.title: ScreenConnect Attacks Target at Least 288 Endpoints Across 48 Organizations With Rogue Clients
strikes.location: Organizations using ConnectWise ScreenConnect managed via partner environments; ground zero spans multiple victim organizations, vendor headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, USA.
strikes.data_affected: Endpoints and systems managed via ScreenConnect remote access clients across affected partner organizations; specific data exfiltrated not disclosed.
strikes.impact: At least 288 endpoints across 48 organizations were compromised via rogue ScreenConnect clients; five third-party extensions were forcibly disabled in partner environments as a containment measure.
strikes.prevention: Enforce strict allowlisting of authorized remote access clients and audit third-party extensions for anomalous or unauthorized ScreenConnect client deployments in managed environments.
strikes.summary: Attackers deployed rogue ScreenConnect clients to gain unauthorized access to at least 288 endpoints across 48 organizations. ConnectWise disabled five third-party partner extensions as a precaution, stating the incident does not appear to involve a compromise of its own infrastructure or a vulnerability in ScreenConnect itself.

strikes.title: Fandango says hackers stole payment card details from checkout pages
strikes.location: Fandango Media's online checkout pages (Fandango Media LLC, headquartered in the United States).
strikes.data_affected: Payment card details (e.g., card numbers, expiration dates, CVV codes) entered by customers on Fandango's checkout pages.
strikes.impact: Fandango Media customers who entered payment card information on the checkout pages were affected; the full scale and number of affected individuals were not disclosed in the report.
strikes.prevention: Implement real-time integrity monitoring and Content Security Policy (CSP) headers on all checkout pages to detect and block unauthorized script injection (e-skimming/Magecart-style attacks).
strikes.summary: Ticket seller Fandango Media suffered a data breach in which hackers injected malicious code into its checkout pages to steal customers' payment card details. Fandango is notifying affected customers of the compromise.

strikes.title: FBI warns ARTEX AI hacking tool is powering global cyberattacks
strikes.location: ConnectWise (US-headquartered managed service provider) as the supply-chain entry point, with downstream impact on Microsoft 365 customer environments worldwide.
strikes.data_affected: Microsoft 365 customer environments accessed via the compromised ConnectWise supply-chain; full scope of data exfiltrated not disclosed.
strikes.impact: Multiple organizations using ConnectWise-managed Microsoft 365 environments were compromised; the scale is described as global, though precise victim counts were not disclosed.
strikes.prevention: Enforce strict third-party vendor access controls and continuously monitor privileged remote management tools like ConnectWise for anomalous automation activity consistent with AI-driven attack frameworks.
strikes.summary: Hackers leveraged an AI-powered penetration testing framework called ARTEX to automate a supply-chain breach against ConnectWise, compromising downstream Microsoft 365 customer environments. The FBI issued a warning attributing the attack to this tool as part of a broader pattern of global cyberattacks.

strikes.title: TSMC employee data breach linked to cloud provider
strikes.location: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), headquartered in Hsinchu, Taiwan — breach originated via a third-party cloud provider.
strikes.data_affected: Personal employee data (~6.9 GB), including details not fully disclosed in the report, sourced from a third-party cloud provider used by TSMC.
strikes.impact: TSMC employees' personal data was exposed and put up for auction; the breach affected TSMC's workforce data but was attributed to a third-party cloud provider, not TSMC's core infrastructure directly. Full scale of affected individuals not disclosed.
strikes.prevention: Enforce strict third-party vendor security assessments and contractual data-handling obligations, including mandatory encryption of employee data at rest and in transit across all cloud providers.
strikes.summary: TSMC confirmed that personal employee data was leaked after a threat actor listed approximately 6.9 GB of allegedly stolen information for auction online. The breach was linked to a third-party cloud provider rather than TSMC's own systems.

strikes.title: Cursor confirms security breach led to malicious Claude Code extension
strikes.location: Cursor's AI-powered code editor marketplace, United States
strikes.data_affected: Credentials belonging to Fireworks AI; Cursor marketplace integrity — a malicious Claude Code extension was injected into the official extension marketplace.
strikes.impact: Cursor marketplace users who installed the malicious Claude Code extension were exposed to a trojanized developer tool; the full scope of downstream user impact was not disclosed in the report.
strikes.prevention: Enforce short-lived, scoped API credentials with anomaly-based access monitoring for all third-party AI infrastructure providers, and implement cryptographic signing and automated integrity verification for all marketplace extensions before publication.
strikes.summary: Cursor confirmed a security breach in which attackers stole credentials from AI infrastructure provider Fireworks AI to gain access to Cursor's marketplace and distribute a malicious Claude Code extension to users. The compromise allowed threat actors to trojanize a developer tool and push it through an official, trusted distribution channel.

strikes.title: Trezor confirms crypto-stealing implants in three wallets, releases fix
strikes.location: Southeast Asia — via CryptoBilis, a regional Trezor hardware wallet reseller
strikes.data_affected: Cryptocurrency wallet recovery phrases (seed phrases) stored on tampered Trezor Safe 5 hardware wallets.
strikes.impact: At least three confirmed end-customers who purchased Trezor Safe 5 wallets through the CryptoBilis reseller in Southeast Asia were exposed to full cryptocurrency theft via exfiltrated recovery phrases; broader scale of affected units not disclosed.
strikes.prevention: Purchase hardware wallets exclusively from the manufacturer's official store or verified authorized resellers, and verify device integrity using the manufacturer's authenticity check tools upon receipt before use.
strikes.summary: Three Trezor Safe 5 hardware wallets sold by Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis were found to contain malicious hardware implants designed to steal wallet recovery phrases and transmit them to attackers via cellular networks. Trezor confirmed the tampering and released a firmware fix to address the compromise.

strikes.title: German military drone operations disrupted by cyberattack
strikes.location: Quantum Systems GmbH, Munich, Germany
strikes.data_affected: Systems supporting military drone operations; full scope of compromised data or systems not disclosed.
strikes.impact: Quantum Systems' drone operations were disrupted; broader operational or mission-level fallout for the German military's use of those drones was not fully disclosed.
strikes.prevention: Implement network segmentation between IT corporate infrastructure and operational technology (OT) systems controlling drone platforms, combined with anomaly-based intrusion detection on OT networks to isolate and contain hostile actors before operational disruption occurs.
strikes.summary: German defense technology company Quantum Systems confirmed it detected a cyberattack by "hostile actors" in late October that disrupted its military drone operations. The company acknowledged the incident was part of an active, targeted attack campaign against its systems.

strikes.title: Lithuanian customs agency restores services after cyberattack, possible data breach
strikes.location: Lithuanian Customs (Muitinės departamentas), Lithuania
strikes.data_affected: User management portal systems; possible breach of user/account data (scope not disclosed)
strikes.impact: Lithuanian Customs operations were disrupted, with the main user management portal taken offline temporarily; the scale of any data exposure was not disclosed.
strikes.prevention: Implement network segmentation and access controls to isolate user management portals, limiting attackers' ability to pivot and forcing temporary full shutdowns in future incidents.
strikes.summary: On November 10, Lithuanian Customs suffered a cyberattack that forced the temporary shutdown of its main user management portal. Services were progressively restored over the following weekend, though a possible data breach is under investigation.

strikes.title: New GitDoor and GraphDoor Backdoors Turn GitHub and SharePoint Into Covert C2 Channels
strikes.location: Government sector organizations across multiple countries in Asia and Africa (specific nations not disclosed).
strikes.data_affected: Government networks and systems; command-and-control communications routed covertly through Microsoft SharePoint and GitHub infrastructure.
strikes.impact: Government sector organizations across multiple countries in Asia and Africa were compromised; the full scale of data exfiltration or operational disruption was not disclosed in the report.
strikes.prevention: Implement strict egress filtering and behavioral monitoring to detect anomalous outbound traffic to legitimate cloud services (e.g., SharePoint, GitHub) being abused as C2 channels, supplemented by application allowlisting on government endpoints.
strikes.summary: An active cyber intrusion campaign dubbed Operation ShadowCloud has been targeting government sectors across Asia and Africa using two previously undocumented backdoors — GitDoor and GraphDoor — which abuse Microsoft SharePoint and GitHub as covert command-and-control channels. Kaspersky identified the campaign in early 2026.

strikes.title: Hijacked Optimizely Scripts Served Card Skimmer and iOS Exploit Kits to CNN, BBC and Zoom Visitors
strikes.location: Optimizely Web Experimentation platform (US-headquartered SaaS vendor), with malicious script delivery cascading to websites of 178+ customer organizations globally.
strikes.data_affected: Third-party JavaScript scripts served by Optimizely Web Experimentation; payment card data targeted via skimmer; iOS device integrity targeted via exploit kit delivered to end-user visitors.
strikes.impact: At least 178 customer organizations, including high-profile names such as CNN, BBC, and Zoom, had malicious code silently delivered to their website visitors. End-users across these sites were exposed to credential/card-harvesting skimmer code and an iOS exploit kit; the full scale of individual victim compromise was not disclosed.
strikes.prevention: Implement Subresource Integrity (SRI) hashes for all third-party scripts so that browsers reject any tampered script before execution, preventing injected malicious code from running even if the upstream CDN or platform is compromised.
strikes.summary: An attacker exploited a vulnerability in Optimizely Web Experimentation to inject malicious code into scripts served by the platform to its customers' websites. Visitors to at least 178 affected organizations — including CNN, BBC, and Zoom — were exposed to a card skimmer and iOS exploit kit delivered via the hijacked scripts.

strikes.title: Japan takes Fugaku supercomputer offlline after cyberattack
strikes.location: RIKEN Center for Computational Science, Kobe, Japan
strikes.data_affected: Systems and operational environment of the Fugaku supercomputer; specific data exfiltrated or compromised not disclosed.
strikes.impact: The Fugaku supercomputer — a critical national research asset — was forced offline, disrupting computational science operations at RIKEN. Full scope of the breach and downstream research impact not disclosed.
strikes.prevention: Implement strict network segmentation and privileged access controls around high-performance computing (HPC) infrastructure, combined with continuous anomaly detection to identify unauthorized access before system integrity is compromised.
strikes.summary: Japan's Fugaku supercomputer, operated by the RIKEN Center for Computational Science, was taken offline following a confirmed security breach. The incident forced a shutdown of one of the world's most powerful supercomputers to contain the compromise.

strikes.title: Researchers hijack Hugging Face account for popular Kokoro AI model
strikes.location: Hugging Face AI model-hosting platform (ground zero); model consumed by downstream projects at major US-based cloud and chip vendors.
strikes.data_affected: The Hugging Face repository and model weights for the Kokoro text-to-speech model; account ownership and publishing controls for that model.
strikes.impact: The Kokoro model is integrated into AI projects across at least five major technology companies (Google, NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, AWS). A malicious version of the same takeover could have delivered backdoored or trojanized model weights to all downstream consumers, potentially affecting a large but not-fully-disclosed number of production systems and users.
strikes.prevention: Hugging Face should enforce cryptographic or verified ownership controls (e.g., signed commits, two-factor confirmation of namespace transfers, and mandatory account identity verification) before allowing any party to claim or modify the ownership of a popular model repository.
strikes.summary: Security researchers exploited a lack of ownership verification on the Hugging Face platform to fully hijack the account hosting Kokoro, a widely used open-source text-to-speech AI model. The takeover demonstrated that a malicious actor could have substituted or poisoned the model, compromising downstream projects at Google, NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, and AWS.

strikes.title: Tor releases emergency update amid ongoing DDoS attack
strikes.location: Tor Project network infrastructure (relay layer), headquartered in Seattle, Washington, USA.
strikes.data_affected: Tor network relay infrastructure; relay availability and performance degraded network-wide.
strikes.impact: Most Tor relay operators affected; network relays overwhelmed, likely degrading anonymized browsing and onion-service availability for the broader Tor user base globally. Full scale of user impact not specifically disclosed.
strikes.prevention: Deploy rate-limiting and proof-of-work challenge mechanisms at relay entry points to throttle high-volume, unauthenticated DDoS traffic before it can saturate relay capacity.
strikes.summary: The Tor Project issued an emergency security update for its network relay software in response to an ongoing DDoS attack that overwhelmed relays and impacted the majority of Tor relay operators. The attack prompted the organization to release hardened defenses out-of-band to stabilize the network.

strikes.title: Uber notifies drivers of data breach affecting nearly 150,000 people
strikes.location: Fireworks AI (AI infrastructure provider), United States — the system breached that held Uber driver data.
strikes.data_affected: Personal data of approximately 150,000 Uber drivers, held by third-party AI infrastructure provider Fireworks AI; exact fields (e.g., names, contact details, license information) not fully disclosed in the report.
strikes.impact: Approximately 150,000 Uber drivers had their personal data stolen; Uber issued formal breach notifications to those individuals. Broader operational or financial fallout was not disclosed.
strikes.prevention: Enforce strict third-party vendor data minimization and access controls — ensure AI infrastructure providers store only the minimum necessary customer data, undergo regular security assessments, and are contractually bound to rapid breach disclosure to limit downstream exposure.
strikes.summary: Attackers breached Fireworks AI, an AI infrastructure provider used by Uber, in early October and stole data belonging to nearly 150,000 Uber drivers. Uber began notifying the affected drivers of the breach during the reporting window of November 2026.

strikes.title: Optimizely hack infected CNN, Fox News, BBC, Salesforce sites with malware
strikes.location: Optimizely's platform (vendor headquartered in the United States), with malicious reach across globally prominent customer websites.
strikes.data_affected: Visitor cryptocurrency wallet data, payment card information, and iOS device exposure via malicious JavaScript payloads injected through Optimizely's platform.
strikes.impact: Potentially millions of end-users visiting major global websites (CNN, Fox News, BBC, Salesforce, GitLab, Zoom, and others) were exposed to credential- and crypto-stealing scripts and iOS exploit code; the full scope of victim organisations and affected user count was not disclosed.
strikes.prevention: Implement Subresource Integrity (SRI) checks on all third-party JavaScript dependencies so that any tampered or unauthorised script is blocked by the browser before execution.
strikes.summary: A suspected supply chain attack on Optimizely, a widely used digital experience platform, resulted in malicious JavaScript being injected into numerous high-profile websites including CNN, Fox News, BBC, Salesforce, GitLab, and Zoom. Visitors to these sites were exposed to scripts designed to steal cryptocurrency and payment information, as well as exploit vulnerabilities in iOS devices.

strikes.title: Uber says nearly 150,000 impacted by third-party breach
strikes.location: United States — Uber Technologies Inc. (headquartered in San Francisco, California), breach originating at an unnamed third-party service provider.
strikes.data_affected: Internal credentials and personal data of approximately 150,000 individuals; exact data categories not fully disclosed in the report.
strikes.impact: Approximately 150,000 individuals were impacted; the breach originated at an unnamed third-party service provider, with Uber's account subsequently accessed using the stolen credentials.
strikes.prevention: Enforce strict third-party vendor access controls, including short-lived credentials, privileged access management (PAM), and continuous monitoring of vendor-held credentials to detect and revoke compromised access immediately.
strikes.summary: A third-party service provider notified Uber on October 9 that internal credentials were stolen and used to access Uber's account, exposing data belonging to nearly 150,000 individuals. Uber disclosed the breach via notification letters to affected parties.

strikes.title: Website management platform Optimizely confirms hackers put malicious code into customer sites
strikes.location: Optimizely Web Experimentation platform, affecting customer websites globally; Optimizely is headquartered in New York, USA.
strikes.data_affected: Customer-facing website code; malicious JavaScript was inserted into sites managed through the Optimizely Web Experimentation platform — specific data exfiltrated from end users not disclosed.
strikes.impact: At least 178 widely visited customer websites were compromised with malicious JavaScript, potentially exposing their end users to malicious code execution; full scope of visitor impact not disclosed.
strikes.prevention: Implement Sub-Resource Integrity (SRI) checks and a strict Content Security Policy (CSP) on all third-party scripts loaded from platform vendors, so any unauthorized script modifications are blocked or flagged before executing in end-user browsers.
strikes.summary: Hackers injected malicious JavaScript code into 178 widely visited websites running on Optimizely's Web Experimentation platform. Optimizely confirmed the breach, which allowed attackers to distribute malicious code to downstream customer sites via the platform.

strikes.title: British hacker who stole $11m through text message scheme jailed for six years in US
strikes.location: United States (victims and prosecution); perpetrator based in Dundee, Scotland, UK
strikes.data_affected: Victim cryptocurrency holdings and financial accounts, accessed via SIM-swapping attacks that hijacked phone numbers to bypass multi-factor authentication.
strikes.impact: Multiple victims defrauded of a combined $11 million; Buchanan received a six-year US federal prison sentence, confirming the scale and criminal seriousness of the scheme. Scattered Spider is described as a notorious group with a broad pattern of similar attacks.
strikes.prevention: Telecommunications providers and account holders should disable SMS-based multi-factor authentication in favour of hardware security keys or authenticator apps, which cannot be intercepted via SIM-swapping.
strikes.summary: Tyler Buchanan, a British national from Dundee and member of the Scattered Spider hacking group, was sentenced to six years in a US prison for orchestrating a text-message-based SIM-swapping scheme that stole approximately $11 million. Buchanan, who began hacking as a teenager, was convicted in the United States.

strikes.title: Hackers Breach N-able Cloud Server, Disrupting Email Security Management Across 3 Regions
strikes.location: N-able's Mail Assure and Spam Experts Hosted Cloud server environment
strikes.data_affected: Cloud server infrastructure supporting Mail Assure and Spam Experts Hosted Cloud; management interfaces and APIs were taken offline as a containment measure — specific data exfiltrated not disclosed.
strikes.impact: Email security management services were disrupted for customers across three unspecified regions; the full scope of affected customers and any data exposure was not disclosed at the time of reporting.
strikes.prevention: Restrict and harden access to cloud management interfaces and APIs through network segmentation, IP allowlisting, and mandatory multi-factor authentication to reduce the attack surface on hosted cloud infrastructure.
strikes.summary: Unknown threat actors gained unauthorized access to a server within N-able's Mail Assure and Spam Experts Hosted Cloud infrastructure. In response, N-able disabled management interfaces and APIs, disrupting email security management services across three regions.

strikes.title: New EggStreme Malware Variant Goes Silent to Evade Security Tools in Government Attacks
strikes.location: Government organizations in the Philippines
strikes.data_affected: Government networks and systems in the Philippines; specific data exfiltrated not disclosed.
strikes.impact: Philippine government organizations are actively targeted; the persistent campaign continues despite prior exposure, suggesting prolonged unauthorized access. Full operational impact and number of compromised entities not disclosed.
strikes.prevention: Deploy behavior-based and memory-forensic endpoint detection that identifies malware by runtime behavior and code patterns rather than static file hashes, neutralizing the threat actor's recompilation-based evasion strategy.
strikes.summary: A suspected Chinese APT group has rebuilt its EggStreme malware toolkit — recompiling binaries and rotating infrastructure — to evade detection while continuing to target government organizations in the Philippines. Bitdefender's technical analysis revealed the retooling strategy, noting that cheap operational pivots such as recompilation and new domains allow the group to persist despite prior exposure.

strikes.title: Hackers Exploiting Critical Puppet RCE Flaw Affecting Enterprise Management Servers
strikes.location: Perforce Puppet enterprise management servers globally (vendor headquartered in the United States)
strikes.data_affected: Perforce Puppet enterprise infrastructure-as-code and configuration management servers; systems and configurations managed via Puppet are potentially accessible to attackers upon exploitation.
strikes.impact: Enterprise organizations using Perforce Puppet for infrastructure management are affected; successful exploitation could grant attackers remote code execution on management servers, potentially compromising entire managed infrastructure fleets. Scale of affected victims not disclosed beyond CISA's broad advisory.
strikes.prevention: Apply Perforce Puppet vendor-issued patches for CVE-2026-115731 immediately, and restrict network access to Puppet master/enterprise servers to trusted hosts only, following CISA's KEV remediation deadlines.
strikes.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-115731, a critical remote code execution flaw (CVSS 9.4) in Perforce Puppet's enterprise infrastructure-as-code and configuration management platform, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog following reports of active in-the-wild exploitation. The vulnerability affects enterprise management servers, posing significant risk to organizations relying on Puppet for infrastructure automation.

strikes.title: Attackers Compromise Microsoft's Agent Framework PyPI Package to Steal Cloud Credentials
strikes.location: Microsoft's agent-framework package on the Python Package Index (PyPI), affecting global downstream users of the package.
strikes.data_affected: Cloud credentials of downstream users and systems running the compromised agent-framework Python package.
strikes.impact: Any developer or organization that installed versions 1.26.1 or 1.26.2 of the Microsoft agent-framework PyPI package was exposed to automatic credential theft on Python startup. The full scale of downstream victims was not disclosed at time of reporting, though multiple security vendors (Aikido, Chainguard, Endor Labs, OX Security, SafeDep, Socket, StepSecurity, and Wiz) independently flagged the compromise.
strikes.prevention: Implement automated PyPI package integrity monitoring and dependency pinning with cryptographic hash verification, so that unexpected new package versions are flagged and blocked before being pulled into builds or runtime environments.
strikes.summary: Threat actors compromised Microsoft's agent-framework PyPI package, publishing malicious versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 on November 17, 2026, within 33 minutes of each other. The trojanized packages were designed to execute a credential stealer targeting cloud credentials on every Python interpreter start.

strikes.title: Russian COLD RELIC Hackers Use Stolen Google Workspace Data to Breach Second U.S. Organization
strikes.location: United States — two unnamed U.S.-based organizations targeted in a chained cloud intrusion.
strikes.data_affected: Google Workspace account data and cloud credentials stolen from the first compromised U.S. organization, subsequently used to access systems at a second U.S. organization.
strikes.impact: At least two U.S.-based organizations were compromised in a linked intrusion chain; the initial cloud compromise served as a launchpad for a third-party breach, indicating lateral escalation across organizational boundaries. Full scope of data exfiltrated not disclosed.
strikes.prevention: Enforce strict cross-tenant access controls and conditional access policies within Google Workspace, including mandatory re-authentication, hardware security key MFA, and least-privilege service account scoping to prevent stolen credentials from being reused to pivot into third-party environments.
strikes.summary: The Russia-linked threat group Cold Relic (formerly COLDRIVER/UNC4057) weaponized stolen Google Workspace data from an initial U.S. organization compromise to pivot and breach a second U.S. organization, in a chained intrusion campaign investigated by Google's Mandiant and GTIG in 2026.

strikes.title: Ukraine, FBI arrest ransomware gang members tied to $40M in ransoms
strikes.location: Ukraine (arrest location; gang operated internationally targeting companies worldwide)
strikes.data_affected: Corporate systems and data of at least 28 victim companies worldwide; specific data types not disclosed.
strikes.impact: At least 28 companies across multiple countries were victimized, with a combined ransom payout exceeding $40.5 million. Four suspected gang members were arrested in Ukraine.
strikes.prevention: Maintain offline, immutable backups and a tested incident-response plan so that ransom payment becomes unnecessary even when systems are encrypted.
strikes.summary: Ukrainian authorities, in coordination with the FBI, arrested four suspected members of an international ransomware gang responsible for extorting at least 28 companies worldwide. The group is linked to more than $40.5 million in ransom payments.

strikes.title: Data breach impacts 40 Irish credit unions in reported IT provider hack
strikes.location: Wellington IT (IT service provider), serving credit unions predominantly based in Ireland.
strikes.data_affected: Sensitive personal and financial information belonging to members of approximately 50 credit unions.
strikes.impact: Roughly 50 credit unions were affected — the majority of which are located in Ireland — with their members' sensitive data exposed as a result of the compromise of their shared IT provider, Wellington IT.
strikes.prevention: Enforce rigorous third-party vendor security requirements, including mandatory security audits, network segmentation between provider and client environments, and contractual incident-response obligations, to limit blast radius when a shared IT supplier is compromised.
strikes.summary: A cyberattack on Wellington IT, an IT service provider for credit unions, exposed sensitive member data belonging to customers of approximately 50 credit unions, with the majority of affected institutions based in Ireland. The breach is attributed to a hack of the IT provider rather than the credit unions directly.

strikes.title: Microsoft’s Agent Framework PyPI package compromised to steal credentials
strikes.location: PyPI (Python Package Index) — Microsoft's official Agent Framework package repository listing; developers worldwide consuming the package.
strikes.data_affected: Cloud credentials and other sensitive information stored on developers' systems; the integrity of two published versions of the Agent Framework PyPI package.
strikes.impact: Developers who installed or updated the compromised versions of the Agent Framework package were exposed to credential theft. The breadth of impact was not disclosed, but any developer or organization consuming the affected package versions from PyPI was potentially affected.
strikes.prevention: Implement dependency integrity verification using cryptographic hash pinning (e.g., pinning exact package hashes in requirements files) and monitor PyPI package updates for unexpected behavioral changes or new maintainer activity before deploying to production environments.
strikes.summary: Hackers compromised Microsoft's official Agent Framework Python package on PyPI, publishing two malicious versions that harvested cloud credentials and other sensitive data from developers' systems. The attack targeted the software supply chain by poisoning a trusted, widely-used Microsoft-published package.

strikes.title: Apache warns of Roller RCE vulnerability exploited in attacks
strikes.location: Apache Roller servers globally; vulnerability originates in software maintained by the Apache Software Foundation (US-based).
strikes.data_affected: Server-side code execution capabilities on vulnerable Apache Roller instances; underlying host systems potentially fully compromised.
strikes.impact: Any organization or individual running an unpatched Apache Roller server is at risk of complete server compromise. Scale of confirmed victims not disclosed, but active exploitation indicates a broad, ongoing campaign across multiple targets worldwide.
strikes.prevention: Apply Apache's released security patch for the Roller RCE vulnerability immediately; if patching is not immediately possible, restrict network access to Roller instances to trusted IP ranges only.
strikes.summary: Threat actors are actively exploiting a critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability in Apache Roller, a Java-based blog server platform, to gain unauthorized code execution on vulnerable servers. Apache has released security updates to remediate the flaw.
